schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE ACTIVITY (
    PLAYER_ID INT,
    EVENT_DATE DATE,
    DEVICE_ID INT,
    GAMES_PLAYED INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE),
    CHECK (GAMES_PLAYED >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN (TEMP.MIN_DATE + 1) = A.EVENT_DATE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(DISTINCT TEMP.PLAYER_ID)), 2) AS FRACTION FROM (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS MIN_DATE FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) AS TEMP JOIN ACTIVITY AS A ON TEMP.PLAYER_ID = A.PLAYER_ID
q2: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN A.PLAYER_ID IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END)/COUNT(TMP.PLAYER_ID)*1.0,2)AS FRACTION FROM (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS FIRST_DATE FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY 1) TMP LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE FROM ACTIVITY) A ON TMP.PLAYER_ID=A.PLAYER_ID AND DATEDIFF(A.EVENT_DATE,TMP.FIRST_DATE)=1

explanation: Both queries compute the fraction of players who have an event exactly one day after their first event date. Q1 counts such events across all players' activity rows, while Q2 uses a LEFT JOIN to count matching events per player. Given the unique constraint on (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE), both approaches yield the same numerator (number of players with such an event) and denominator (total players).
